about: Variation catalog. Every video picks one value per axis. `feature` and `persona` values come from the studio brand profile. Weights set how much each axis counts toward novelty. Length follows the content: comprehension comes before brevity, and every video stays under 45 seconds.

hook.how: Open on a number that hurts or thrills: a score, a rank, a price, a streak.
"POV: ..." puts the viewer inside a specific, relatable moment.
Ask the question the audience argues about. Answer it by the end.
A confident, defensible claim that makes the viewer want to disagree.
"Stop doing X." Name a common habit and show why it costs them.
Show the painful before and the clean after within the first two seconds.
A visible clock or deadline creates urgency from frame one.
"3 moves that ..." promises a payoff the viewer stays for.
"Can the AI ...?" A bet or test with a reveal.
A first-person admission: "I finished last. Then ..."
Two ways to do the job, side by side. The old way loses.
"The trick nobody uses": a specific, non-obvious tactic.
Open on a reaction: a group chat, a notification storm, a rival's message.
"Pick one." Pause for a beat, then reveal what the product picked and why.

format.how: Stakes, the ask, the product thinking, the answer, the win.
Numbered tips or moves, one per bar, each with a UI proof.
A first-person scenario told in on-screen text and UI moments.
One feature, shown deeply: input, what it considers, output, result.
One number or chart that tells the whole story, animated as data viz.
Split-screen or alternating beats: the old way against the product.
A race against a visible timer; the product beats the clock.
Present options, hold a beat for the guess, reveal with reasoning.
How to do one job in three steps, fast, with the real UI.
A familiar meme structure rebuilt in the brand's motion language.
Alternate myth and fact cards, each landing on a beat.
Tease a feature or update with partial reveals and a clear CTA.

world.how: A 3D line-art world from the app's domain (a court, a pitch, a track, a kitchen grid).
An abstract glowing grid floor with rings; data as landscape.
The product UI on a floating phone or cards, camera moving across screens.
Typography carries everything; minimal UI, maximal type motion.
Bars, lines, and numbers building and morphing as the main visual.
Two panes in contrast, wiping and trading focus on beats.
Notifications, messages, and alerts stacking and resolving.
Product cards floating in depth with parallax and rack focus.
Magazine-style layout: big numerals, rules, captions, generous space.
A path or route drawing across a map-like plane to a destination.
Technical drawing style: dimension lines, callouts, measured reveals.

camera.how: One continuous camera move through the world for the whole piece.
Cut on bar downbeats; each cut changes framing decisively and the new frame holds long enough to read.
Whip pans with motion blur carry the big transitions (two or three per video, about 0.5 s each); calm holds in between.
Punch-in zooms on the key word or number of a scene, synced to hits, then hold.
A mostly static poster frame; motion lives in the elements.
Slow layered drift with depth, calm pacing, premium feel.
The camera circles a subject or the world's center.
Vertical moves: rising reveals, top-down drops.

music.how: Half-time trap: syncopated kicks, clap on 3, hat rolls, 808.
Cowbell melody, heavy 808, dark minor progression.
Four on the floor, offbeat open hats, bright chords.
Sliding 808s, skippy hats, tense minor harmony.
Soft keys, vinyl, lazy swing; calm, clever, explanatory.
Punchy kick and snare, head-nod groove, confident.
Breakbeat energy at double time; keep scene changes on bar lines so the picture stays readable.
Bright, maximal, glitchy; playful and loud.
Driving chant beat: a hit on every beat for rapid-fire lists.
No music: crisp UI clicks, whooshes, and tones carry the rhythm.

cta.how: Logo, one line, and the URL as a button.
Point to the link in bio with a clear reason to tap.
"Comment X" to get a resource or answer; drives comments.
"Follow for part 2" or a recurring series name.
End on a question the audience will answer in comments.
"Save this for Sunday": utility content worth bookmarking.

palette.how: The brand's dark surfaces with accent highlights.
Light surfaces; switch the world to multiply blending.
Full-bleed brand color moments for the biggest beats.
Near-monochrome with one accent color doing all the work.

length.how: One idea: a single stat, one before and after, or one tip. Hook, the idea, the end card.
Hook, two or three proofs at about 4 s each, payoff, end card. The template is 24 s (12 bars at 120 BPM).
A story or a list of three with room to breathe: 4 to 5 s per idea. 16 bars at 128 BPM is 30 s.
Walkthroughs and tutorials with several steps. The ceiling: every video stays under 45 s.

ending.how: Resolve on the brand end card.
The last frame flows into the first so the video rewatches itself.
End mid-reveal to set up the next episode.
Land a joke or a twist, then a quick logo sting.
